newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Santos says deregulation benefits overrated.
newsitem.headline: Santos says deregulation benefits overrated.

text.p: Oil and gas company Santos Ltd said on Thursday the benefits of deregulation and reform of the Australian electricity, gas and water industries to the economy were being highly exaggerated.

Santos principal gas marketer John Tidd told a conference on gas reform in the state of Victoria that the Australian government's key industry adviser, the Industry Commission, claimed deregulation would lead to estimated 1.5 percent increase in Australia's gross domestic product (GDP).
"The increase in GDP is certainly there but most of it will be realised even if there was no reform," Tidd said.
Tidd said he believed Professor John Quiggen of James Cook University's estimate that only five percentage of the 1.5 percent growth forecast would truly be the result of deregulation.
"Perhaps, in his assessment, Professor Quiggin goes too far but in the upstream gas business business I believe he is closer to the mark than was the Industry Commission," he said.
Tidd said he looked at reform and deregulation more as a means to an end in that it should ensure Santos was viable and operating at the highest level of efficiency.

"We need to deliver over a long period the right product at the right time at the right price rather than delivering some huge economic benefit to the nation's bottom line that may be short lived," Tidd said.

Santos is one of Australia's largest natural gas producers and owns a majority interest in the Cooper Basin gas and condensate fields which overlap South Australia and Queensaland in central Australia.
Santos owns 59.75 percent of the Cooper Basin unit, Exxin Corp's owns 20.21 percent, Boral Ltd 13.19 percent, Clyde Petroleum Plc CDP.L 4.75 percent and Basin Oil NL 2.1 percent.
